IDE OF PRACTICE FOR DEMOLITION OF BUILDINGS YEAR 2004

-

5.9 Underground Structures

5.9.1 General
The adverse effects of demolition warks to any building, structure, land, street or service are to be studied.
A monitoring plan should be provided if necessary. It may include, but not be limited to, the following: -

1. Monitoring stations {including, but not limited to, settlement check points, tilting and vibration check
points) for detailed monitoring of movement and vibration in any building, structure, land, street or
underground seryice should be provided throughout the demolition period. Refer to PAP APP-24 &
APP-131, Schedule Area No. 3 for the trigger levels of a monitoring station, The vibration control can
make reference to PNAP APP-137;

2, Plezometers for the detailed monitoring of ground water conditions;

3, Inclinometer for the detailed monitoring of lateral movement of existing retaining structures (e.9.,
screen wail, pile wall or diaphragm wall):

4. The frequency at which readings will be recorded or taken;

5. The alert, alarm and action levels of the monitoring stations and contingency measures ta be taken
should be agreed upon with the Building Authority and concerned utility undertakers.

§.9.2 Demolition Method
Refer to Section 4 of the EH for the demolition method of various structural elements, Effects on adjacent
structures are to be studied,

5.9.3 Guidelines
1A) Overall Stability
In addition to maintain the stability of the remaining parts of the buildings, the uplifting checking
should fulfill the requirements as stated In Clause 1[c) of Paragraph 15 Part lll of Building
(Construction) Regulations (CAP. 123). Refer also to paragraph 2.5.4 (b} of Code of Practice for
Foundations.

(B) Shoring
Assess the movement of adjacent bullding structures, land, street or services inearly design stages
in order to determine a suitable demolition method and precautionary measures. The condition of
a building's structure shall be verified if the floors or part of the building structure act as propping
to the retaining structures,

(c) Dewatering
Dewatering should be avoided during demolition works. In case dewatering |s required, the
engineer should submit a proposal with Excavation and Lateral support Works or Foundation Works
for Building Autherity’s approval,

Please also refer to PNAP APP-22 on dewatering.

(D) Existing Foundation
The re-use of existing foundations should be considered in the foundation submission if applicable.

(E) Site Security and Safety
AP/RSE/RSC shall plan and implement suitable site security and safety,
